models.title: Reading · the worst road trip ever

block.label: READING · THE WORST ROAD TRIP EVER
block.html:
Last summer, my friends Bruno and Carla set off for the beach at 6 a.m. They weren't worried: the car was new and the weather was perfect. At 8 o'clock, they were driving on the highway and singing when the car broke down. Bruno opened the hood, but he didn't know what to do.

While they were waiting for help, it started to rain. Carla was looking for the umbrella in the luggage when she fell over on the wet road. She wasn't hurt, but she was very angry!

A truck driver stopped and helped them. The problem? They ran out of gas! The car was fine, but Bruno wasn't looking at the fuel gauge. Two hours later, in a traffic jam, Carla said, "Let's turn back." But they didn't. They arrived at 4 p.m., and the sun was shining.

A made-up story.

models.title: Reading · road trip · answer with short answers

block.label: READING · SHORT ANSWERS
block.html: Answer with a short answer and one more sentence. Then reveal.

items.q: Were they driving when the car broke down?
items.a: Yes, they were. They were driving on the highway.

items.q: Was it raining when they set off?
items.a: No, it wasn't. The weather was perfect.

items.q: Was Carla looking for the umbrella when she fell over?
items.a: Yes, she was. It was in the luggage.

items.q: Was Bruno looking at the fuel gauge?
items.a: No, he wasn't. That's why they ran out of gas.

items.q: What was the weather like when they arrived?

lesson.title: Were You Driving? On the Road
lesson.subtitle: Past continuous: negative and question · 8 phrasal verbs · a road trip that went wrong
lesson.plan: Revisão do vocabulário das últimas aulas por perguntas (a noite em que a luz acabou, transporte, quantidades). Past Continuous Tipo 2, como ficou combinado na aula 29: negativo (tabela, afirmativo × negativo, 5 frases) e pergunta (tabela, afirmativo × pergunta, 5 frases, perguntas para o professor). Tema novo: viagem de carro que deu errado, com 8 phrasal verbs (set off, break down, run out of, look for, pick up, get off, turn back, fall over), palavras de estrada, leitura, história para completar, jogo do álibi, conversa e role-play.
